briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 23, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Climate Crisis Frontline: Extreme Phenomena and Warnings
sections.content: Today's climate news begins with a strong warning about unprecedented extreme phenomena and the threats they pose. Domestically, defying the old saying 'Cheoseo Magic' (the end of heat), 'extreme heatwaves' more severe than Daeseo (the hottest period) are continuing. These heatwaves are longer and stronger than in the past, raising the need for expanding urban green spaces and refining forecasts [18, 19]. Such climate change is directly threatening food security, making urgent responses through agricultural technology innovation imperative [4]. Internationally, climate change is described as 'the defining crisis of our time' [38], with a 'global syndemic' combining malnutrition and obesity emerging in the Pacific region, and growing concerns about long-term impacts on the Colorado River [33, 34]. The phenomenon of Halloween items being sold in August suggests that the concept of seasons is being disrupted [40], and Merz, among others, points to climate change as the cause of wildfires [31], indicating a global escalation in the severity of the climate crisis.

sections.title: 🌍 Societal Calls and Financial Responses
sections.content: Social awareness of the severity of this climate crisis is gradually spreading, and calls for immediate action are growing louder. In Sweden, large-scale demonstrations urging immediate action on climate change occurred ahead of the general election, demanding attention and action from political circles [1, 6]. Simultaneously, climate change has now risen beyond a mere environmental issue to become a core agenda item for financial boards, recognized as both a crisis and an opportunity [2, 8]. Businesses are facing various types of risks due to climate change [5], which is having such a widespread impact that it is even changing the role of industries like cosmetics, making them 'survival essentials' [13]. Columnist Kang Cheol-soo stated that in the context of the climate crisis, the Gyeongnam region is not a 'beneficiary region' but rather on the 'frontline of response,' urging proactive regional action [12].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts for a Sustainable Future
sections.content: Even amidst the climate crisis, various domestic and international efforts for a sustainable future are actively underway. Domestically, adaptation efforts in the agricultural sector continue, with Hongcheon County identifying income-generating crops resilient to climate change, and Gyeongsangbuk-do spreading Korean melon cultivation techniques to farms [9, 10, 17]. KEPCO KDN is supporting vulnerable populations with summer relief supplies, striving to mitigate the impacts of climate change together with local communities [16]. The importance of education is also highlighted, with a lecture on climate change successfully concluding at the Ulsan Mathematics Culture Center [14]. Various local governments, including Gwangmyeong City, Daejeon Daedeok-gu, and the Gyeongju Sustainable Development Council, are operating programs to spread a culture of practical action in daily life, such as carbon neutrality experiential education through play and urban wetland cultivation [21, 23, 24, 26, 28]. Internationally, engineers are advocating for a transition to a circular economy, simultaneously seeking climate change solutions and job creation [35]. Positive movements for change are also observed, with U.S. labor unions fighting for good jobs in the clean energy sector [39].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Policy Contradictions and New Economic Opportunities
sections.content: Meanwhile, some contradictory situations are observed in climate change response policies. A contradiction has arisen between the domestic government's 'carbon neutrality' goal and its 'LNG expansion' policy driven by the operation of large-scale mega-projects, raising concerns about the implementation of carbon neutrality [20, 30]. Amidst this situation, the need for preparing countermeasures against climate change is continuously being raised [7], and companies are actively responding to climate change by strengthening their ESG management. Hanwha General Insurance is taking swift steps in cyber and climate change response [11], the Ansan Environmental Foundation is launching an ESG management course [22], and Gwangsan-gu is actively initiating citizen-participatory energy transition jobs linked to carbon neutrality practices [25], demonstrating how businesses and local communities are exploring new economic opportunities [27]. Internationally, climate change is influencing investment strategies, leading to investment discussions focusing on Canada rather than Russia [3], and also offering new economic opportunities by pioneering Arctic shipping routes [32]. Discussions addressing the ripple effects of climate change are active [36], and scientific questions, such as whether atmospheric carbon can be reduced by filling all car tires with CO2 [41], are also being raised, indicating a multifaceted approach.

briefing.closing: Today's climate briefing has once again reminded us of the severity of the climate crisis and the importance of a global response. Confirming the importance of innovation and solidarity for a sustainable future even amidst this crisis, we must not cease our efforts towards a better tomorrow. This concludes today's climate briefing.

summary.phenomenon: With the activation of three major mega-projects, including the Honam semiconductor cluster, a projection emerged that an additional power supply equivalent to 19 large nuclear power plants would be required, prompting the government to pursue the expansion of liquefied natural gas (LNG) power generation.
